title: Teacher professional development for a future with generative artificial intelligence – an integrative literature review
extended_summary:
This paper asks what components should be included in teacher professional development (TPD) for the ethical integration of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) into teaching. The authors frame GenAI as a rapidly expanding technology that creates both opportunities and risks in education, especially around plagiarism, authenticity, privacy, bias, and the preservation of human interaction and critical thinking. Rather than testing an intervention, the paper synthesizes recent literature to identify the knowledge, skills, and pedagogical conditions teachers need in order to guide students in the safe and ethical use of GenAI.

The study is an integrative literature review based on searches in Scopus and Web of Science for publications from 2017 to 2024. After screening, 33 studies were included, with most from higher education and a smaller number from non-higher education contexts. The review draws on research about teachers, students, and educational AI more broadly, and uses this evidence to build a conceptual proposal for TPD. The authors emphasize that teachers need AI literacy, understanding of how AI systems work, awareness of ethical risks, and exposure to hands-on activities that let them try tools, reflect with peers, and adapt strategies to their own teaching context.

The main conclusion is that effective TPD for GenAI should go beyond technical training. It should combine basic AI knowledge, awareness of AI tools and their limitations, ethical reflection, and collaborative design of lesson plans and classroom strategies. The paper also highlights that teachers should know how students are already using GenAI, and that professional learning should help teachers build confidence to use these tools pedagogically while preserving critical thinking, equity, privacy, and meaningful human relationships in learning.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: Generative AI tools are systems that produce new content from user prompts, such as text, images, code, or other outputs, and can also support feedback, tutoring, and adaptive assistance in educational settings.
identified_tools.use_case: This integrative literature review examined generative AI tools in general, focusing on how teachers can use them for ethical and safe instructional practice, including lesson-plan design, classroom implementation, feedback, and coaching-related support.

quality_tier_rationale: This is an integrative literature review and proposal paper, not a primary empirical evaluation of a specific AI tool. It synthesizes prior literature and offers professional-development recommendations rather than reporting original outcome data.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper likely has practical relevance for teacher professional development and classroom implementation, but it does not report measured effects from an intervention. Because no effect sizes or direct outcome data are provided, impact is unclear rather than demonstrated.
